title: Demand shock — headcount & price elasticity playbook (Q1 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc outlines a compact playbook for three demand scenarios (baseline, mild shock, severe shock), ties those scenarios to an actionable headcount plan, and runs a price-elasticity sensitivity matrix to surface revenue/burn outcomes. Intended audience: CFO, Finance business partners, Head of People, GTM leaders.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We model a 12-month horizon starting Jan 2026 across three demand regimes. Baseline assumes flat ARR growth +8% YoY (consistent with current funnel velocity). Mild shock assumes a 20% drop in new ARR for three quarters with slower recover; severe shock assumes a 40% drop and longer recovery. Key levers: (1) targeted hiring freeze in non-customer-facing teams, (2) temporary pause on Dedicated sales capacity expansion, (3) tactical price increases on under-indexed accounts (tiered +7.5%–12.5% depending on contract renewal timing) paired with short-term usage discounts for large customers. Our headline: a calibrated mix of 7% org-wide hiring moderation + selective pricing actions keeps runway within 9–11 months under mild shock and buys 4–6 months under severe shock versus no action.

Assumptions (high level):
- Time horizon: 12 months (Jan 2026–Dec 2026).
- Starting ARR (recurring revenue): $82.5M at 2026-01-01.
- Hosted API revenue mix: 55%; Dedicated/Private: 35%; professional services & other: 10%.
- Gross margin baseline: 68% (post-infra optimizations & caching benefits).
- Avg cost per FTE (loaded): eng = $260k, infra/SRE = $280k, product/PM = $210k, sales/AE = $200k + 12% variable commission, success/CS = $150k, finance/legal/ops = $170k, G&A = $160k.
- Hiring lead times: eng 10–12 weeks, sales 6–8 weeks, CS 6–8 weeks.
- Price elasticity assumptions (initial): small-mid customers E = -1.1, large enterprise E = -0.4. (i.e., small customers more price sensitive).
- Churn reaction to price increases: negligible on enterprise (under negotiated renewals), moderate for self-serve (increase in churn if price > +10%).

Scenario definitions:
1) Baseline: new ARR growth consistent with plan: +8% YoY. No structural cuts; normal hiring cadence.
2) Mild demand shock: new ARR -20% for Q1–Q3 2026 vs plan, rebounds in Q4 with catchup. No one-time headcount layoffs; hiring slows and selective offers paused.
3) Severe demand shock: new ARR -40% for Q1–Q4 2026 vs plan, partial recovery in H1 2027. Requires active cost takeout and hiring freeze; consider limited contractor reductions.

Headcount plan (consolidated view — FTE counts and near-term adjustments):

| Org area            | Baseline FTEs (start) | Baseline hires planned | Mild shock hires (12mo) | Severe shock hires (12mo) | Notes                          |
|---------------------|------------------------|-------------------------|--------------------------|----------------------------|---------------------------------|
| Engineering         | 72                     | +18                    | +6 (deferred)            | +0 (freeze)                | Delay non-critical features     |
| Serving runtime     | 22                     | +6                     | +2                       | 0                          | Prioritize reliability fixes    |
| Infra / SRE         | 18                     | +4                     | +1                       | 0                          | Critical for uptime             |
| Product / PM        | 14                     | +4                     | +1                       | 0                          | Pause new product GTM hires     |
| Sales (AE & SDR)    | 46                     | +12                    | +4                       | -6 (pause + 2 attrition)   | Slow ramp for new capacity      |
| Customer Success    | 30                     | +6                     | +2                       | 0                          | Keep coverage for enterprise    |
| Finance / Legal / Ops| 12                    | +2                     | 0                        | 0                          | Tighten contractors             |
| G&A / Exec          | 8                      | 0                      | 0                        | 0                          | Preserve leadership capacity    |
| Total               | 222                    | +52                    | +16                      | -6                        |                                 |

Notes on HC plan: in mild shock we preserve a small fraction of planned hires to avoid losing product velocity (core infra & priority eng), but defer majority of GTM expansion hires. In severe shock we implement a hiring freeze and consider 12–18 contractor conversions backfill.

Sample loaded cost delta (illustrative, yearly impact):
- Baseline incremental headcount cost (planned hires): 52 hires * avg loaded $205k = ~$10.66M incremental run-rate.
- Mild shock hires: 16 * $205k = ~$3.28M incremental.
- Severe shock: net reduction ( -6 ) * $205k = -$1.23M savings (annualized).

Pricing sensitivity: approach and mechanics
- We segment customers into three buckets: self-serve (SS), SMB / mid-market (MM), and enterprise (ENT).
- Proposed discrete pricing actions:
  a) SS: increase usage-based price per 1k tokens by +10% for new signups and existing on next billing cycle; offer 2-week promo credits to limit churn spike.
  b) MM: targeted +7.5% list price changes at renewal; provide scaled discounts for committed annual contracts.
  c) ENT: pursue contract re-rate for accounts >$500k ARR at +3–5% with added-value package (support/retention SLA).

Elasticity model (summary):
- SS elasticity -1.1: revenue impact = price change * (1 + elasticity * price change). Example: +10% price => -11% volume => net + (1.10 * 0.89) = -? (approx +? see calculations).
- MM elasticity -0.9 (moderate sensitivity).
- ENT elasticity -0.4 (low sensitivity).

Quick sensitivity matrix (annualized revenue delta vs baseline ARR = $82.5M):

Assumptions: SS = 28% of ARR, MM = 37% of ARR, ENT = 35% of ARR.

Case A: Apply SS +10%, MM +7.5%, ENT +4%:
- SS revenue change: +10% price, elasticity -1.1 => volume change -11% -> net SS delta = +10% + (-11%) = -1% roughly -> SS contribution ~0.28 * 82.5M * -1% = -$231k
- MM revenue change: +7.5% price, elasticity -0.9 => volume change -6.75% -> net MM delta = +7.5% - 6.75% = +0.75% -> MM contribution ~0.37 * 82.5M * +0.75% = +$229k
- ENT revenue change: +4% price, elasticity -0.4 => volume change -1.6% -> net ENT delta = +4% - 1.6% = +2.4% -> ENT contribution ~0.35 * 82.5M * +2.4% = +$693k
- Total delta ~ +$691k annually (~+0.84% overall).

Interpretation: a differentiated, modest pricing move can be net accretive if enterprise response is muted and MM are managed via renewals. SS requires careful communication to avoid churn.

Burn and runway impact (simplified):
- Baseline monthly burn (end 2025 run-rate): $3.6M/mo.
- Additional revenue from Case A above ~ $691k/yr -> ~$57.5k/mo, negligible vs fixed burn but helpful.
- Under mild shock (no actions): revenue contraction leads to runway dropping by ~3 months versus baseline. With the pricing actions + hiring moderation outlined above, we recover ~2–3 months of runway.
- Under severe shock, pricing + hiring freeze buys an additional ~4 months but requires more aggressive highway: contractor reductions, delaying non-critical infra, and potentially one-time severance to compress opex quickly if ARR does not stabilize.

Operational playbook (tactical steps):
1) Week 0–4: freeze non-essential job offers except for critical infra/ops; run pricing experiment on 10% of SS cohort (A/B test) and 20% of MM cohort (by renewal window).
2) Week 4–8: evaluate churn delta and revenue delta from experiments; prepare comms templates (billing, support, renewal teams).
3) Month 3: if mild shock persists, implement hiring slowdown + pause new Dedicated region expansion; if severe shock, convene execs for contractor reduction + 1.0 headcount optimization plan.
4) Month 4–6: renegotiate vendor contracts (cloud credits, reserved instances), extend payment terms for large customers if needed to smooth cash flow.

Key risks and monitoring signals:
- Risk: SS churn increase > 8% following price action. Signal: increased trial-to-paid dropoff and higher cancellation rates within 30 days.
- Risk: Enterprise deals delayed -> pipeline aging. Signal: sales cycle length +20% QoQ and closed-won slipping.
- Risk: morale/productivity impact from hiring uncertainty. Signal: voluntary attrition ticks up in engineering/PM.

Dashboard KPIs to track weekly: new ARR by segment, churn by segment (30/90/365), pipeline velocity, offer acceptance rate, average deal size, net dollar retention, runway (months), monthly cash balance.

Decision thresholds (example):
- If new ARR vs plan falls > 15% for two consecutive months -> implement mild shock hiring plan (pause GTM hires).
- If new ARR vs plan falls > 30% for two consecutive months -> escalate to severe shock measures and present reduction scenarios to board.

Open questions / items to resolve (working list):
- Validate elasticity parameters with product analytics owners (Maya) — current assumptions are top-down and need cohort-level lift.
- Confirm exact contract mix with RevOps (Ethan) to identify which enterprise accounts are re-rateable in the near term.
- Build a small workbook (linked) to iterate with variant scenarios (sensitivity sweeps).

Appendix — quick illustrative P&L extract (annualized, rounded):
Baseline (2026 outlook):
- Revenue: $82.5M
- COGS (32%): $26.4M -> Gross profit $56.1M
- Opex (incl. planned hires): $65M -> Operating loss -$8.9M
- Cash runway (starting cash): $110M -> runway ~12 months (baseline)

Mild shock (no action):
- Revenue: $72M (-12.7%)
- COGS: $23M -> GP $49M
- Opex: $63M (slightly lower due to hiring delays) -> Op loss -$14M -> runway ~9 months

Mild shock + actions (pricing + hiring moderation):
- Revenue: $73M
- Opex: $60M -> Op loss -$7M -> runway ~11 months

Severe shock + actions:
- Revenue: $60M
- Opex: $50M (with headcount reductions and contractor cuts) -> Op loss -$? -> runway extended by ~4 months vs no-action severe

Document provenance and next steps:
- This is an internal working doc; please annotate with comments. Finance will publish a cleaned spreadsheet with scenario toggles (see linked artifact). Next review: Feb 27, 2026 — present to execs.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- Focus feedback on elasticity assumptions and which hires we classify as truly mission-critical.
- Suggest labeling any proposed headcount reductions by minimum viable SLA they preserve (customer SLOs).

(End of doc)
